newsitem.title: UK: Abbey National, Pru up after ScotAm deal.
newsitem.headline: Abbey National, Pru up after ScotAm deal.

text.p: Shares in Abbey National Plc rose in early trade on Tuesday as bank stocks rallied from recent weakness and the market welcomed Abbey's failure to win control of insurer Scottish Amicable.

Analysts said there was relief that Abbey had not overpaid for the mutual insurer while Prudential Corp Plc, confirmed as the winning bidder, was seen to be deriving strategic and earnings benefits from the deal.
"Pru has not gone crazy and paid a stupid price," said Michael Lindsay, analyst at Lehman Brothers, "the acquisition looks to be earnings neutral in the first year and enhancing thereafter."
"It is generally good news for the Pru strategically and it they lost it would have been very disappointing. For Abbey there will be relief they did not end up overpaying."
Abbey shares -- which yesterday dropped to a three-month low of 708p -- were up 8-1/2p at 723 by 0824 GMT while the Pru was up 9-1/2p at 549-1/2.
Elsewhere among bank stocks, Lloyds TSB Plc was up 8p at 462, bouncing from a sharp 59p decline in the past four sessions, and Barclays Plc was up 7-1/2p at 998.
National Westminster Bank Plc was up 6p at 682-1/2.

Analysts said the sector, up sharply in the early weeks of the year, had come in for profit-taking as it bore the brunt of fears of rising interest rates, though with Wall Street rallying on Monday there were hopes that a U.S. rate rise had been discounted.
